title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Isolation and Characterization
author: Alaa' Turki, Monawer
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect clinical specimens
steps.instruction: Collect a total of 670 clinical samples from patients attending the main hospitals in Duhok city during the period 8 May 2022 to 28 February 2023.

steps.title: Isolate and identify P. aeruginosa
steps.instruction: Culture the collected specimens, isolate bacterial colonies and identify Pseudomonas aeruginosa using traditional biochemical methods and confirm the identification with a VITEK 2 compact system.

steps.title: Record isolate prevalence
steps.instruction: From the 670 samples, obtain 160 P. aeruginosa isolates distributed as follows: burn 48 (7.17 %), ear 39 (5.82 %), wound 25 (3.73 %), urine 27 (4.03 %), sputum 21 (3.13 %).

steps.title: Test antimicrobial susceptibility
steps.instruction: Perform antimicrobial susceptibility testing on the 160 isolates using standard methods and record resistance rates: tobramycin 64.4 %, gentamicin 57.5 %, amikacin 51.9 %.

steps.title: Select isolates for PCR
steps.instruction: Select 50 of the 160 P. aeruginosa isolates for molecular detection of the aac(6')‑lb gene by conventional PCR.

steps.title: Perform PCR for aac(6')‑lb
steps.instruction: Carry out conventional PCR on the 50 selected isolates using specific primers for the aac(6')‑lb gene (primer sequences not provided).

steps.title: Run agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Separate the PCR products on a 1 % agarose gel, perform electrophoresis, and visualize clear bands of the expected 472 bp size.

steps.title: Confirm PCR positives
steps.instruction: Identify that 46 of the 50 isolates (92 %) are PCR‑positive for the aac(6')‑lb gene based on the 472 bp band.

steps.title: Select samples for sequencing
steps.instruction: Choose 10 of the PCR‑positive isolates for DNA sequencing of the aac(6')‑lb gene.

steps.title: Submit sequences to GenBank
steps.instruction: Submit the obtained sequences to the NCBI BLAST database, record the GenBank accession numbers OQ538204, OQ538205, OQ538206, OQ538207, OQ538208, OQ538209, OQ538210, OQ538211, OQ538212, and OQ538213, and note that the sequences are 99‑100 % identical to reference aac(6')‑lb sequences.
